wu: Students sit in a circle. Teacher whispers a Ramadan-related sentence in Arabic to the first student, e.g., 'I eat suhoor at 4 AM.' They whisper it in English to the next student, who reports it to the next, and so on. The last student says what they heard. Teacher writes the original and final sentence on the board to compare.
wuAlt: Teacher shows 3 flashcards: 'eat suhoor,' 'pray taraweeh,' 'visit family.' Students ask each other 'What did you do yesterday?' and report back to the class.
Teacher writes 5 Ramadan routine verbs on the board. Students stand up and say a sentence about their routine, e.g., 'I always break my fast with dates.' when the teacher claps.
pres: Teacher presents a dialogue on the board: 'Youssef: "I will visit my aunt tonight." Fatima: "He said he would visit his aunt tonight."' Teacher explains 'said' and 'told' + object, and backshift (will → would). Students turn to a partner and practice similar sentences with 'said' and 'told'.
presAlt: Teacher uses a Ramadan story with two characters. Students read short exchanges and rewrite them as reported speech in pairs, with teacher monitoring.
Teacher gives each student a card with a direct speech sentence about Ramadan. They walk around and report what others said, using 'said' or 'told me'.
prac: Students play 'Gossip Chain.' Teacher gives each row a Ramadan sentence to whisper down the line. The last student reports it to the class. Teacher checks for accuracy in reported speech and backshift.
pracAlt: Students work in pairs. One is a 'reporter,' the other a 'source.' The source says a sentence about their Ramadan, and the reporter writes it down correctly.
Teacher writes 5 headlines on the board, e.g., 'Local Mosque Opens Iftar Early.' Students rewrite them as reported speech in their notebooks.
ls: Students listen to a short audio of two people discussing their Ramadan plans. They listen twice and write down 3 sentences in reported speech. Teacher plays the audio again if needed.
re: Teacher says a direct speech sentence about Ramadan, e.g., 'I love eating harira.' Students stand up and shout the reported version, e.g., 'He said he loved eating harira.' The fastest pair gets a point.
prod: Students roleplay 'News Reporters.' One student interviews another about their Ramadan routine using direct speech. The other student reports the interview back to the class in reported speech.
rw: Students read a short dialogue about two friends' Ramadan plans. They then rewrite the dialogue as a paragraph in reported speech, using 'said' and 'told'. Teacher checks for backshift.
st: Teacher tells a short story about a family's Ramadan evening in Morocco. Students reflect on one sentence they would report from the story. Close with: 'Today we learned to report what someone said accurately. Thank you for your participation.'
g: Students whisper a Ramadan sentence down a row, and the last student reports it.
Students find headlines in a text and rewrite them as reported speech.
One student interviews another about Ramadan, and the other reports it back.
Teacher says a sentence, students shout the reported version.
Students rewrite a short dialogue as reported speech.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 3-sentence report about a classmate's Ramadan plans.
Support: Use a sentence frame: 'He said he ________ (verb) ________ (object).'
hw: Write your Ramadan daily routine in 8 sentences using reported speech.
Interview a family member about their Ramadan and report 3 things they said.
Find a news article about Ramadan and rewrite 2 sentences as reported speech.
tip: Use real-life examples from Moroccan Ramadan culture to make reported speech relatable, like reporting what a family member said about suhoor or iftar.
